userStories.title: Project folder selection via CLI argument
userStories.description: As a user, I want to specify a root folder as a command-line argument so that PRDMonitor knows where to look for prd.json files.
acceptanceCriteria: User can pass folder path as a CLI argument (e.g., prdmonitor /path/to/projects)
Application validates that the folder exists and is readable
Default to current directory if no argument provided
Error message printed to stderr if folder is invalid or inaccessible

userStories.title: Subdirectory scanning for prd.json files
userStories.description: As a user, I want the application to scan all subdirectories for prd.json files so that all my projects are discovered automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Application recursively scans subdirectories of the selected folder
Only files named prd.json are detected
Scanning happens on application startup
Number of discovered projects is displayed in the TUI header

userStories.title: JSON parsing and validation
userStories.description: As a user, I want prd.json files to be parsed correctly so that user story data is available for display.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid JSON files are parsed without errors
Project name is extracted from the top-level name field
User stories array is extracted with id, title, description, and status
Malformed JSON files are handled gracefully with error logging

userStories.title: Terminal UI with Kanban board layout
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see a terminal-based Kanban board with Incomplete, In Progress, and Complete columns so that I can visualize status without leaving the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: TUI displays three columns: Incomplete, In Progress, Complete
Columns are clearly labeled with distinct visual styling
Layout adapts to terminal width
Empty columns display a placeholder message
Uses a Go TUI library such as bubbletea or tview

userStories.title: User story card display
userStories.description: As a user, I want each user story displayed as a card showing the id, title, description, and project name so that I can quickly understand what each story is about.
acceptanceCriteria: Each card displays the user story id prominently
Card shows the title in bold or highlighted text
Description is displayed below the title (truncated if needed)
Project name from prd.json name field appears at the top of the card
Cards use box-drawing characters or borders for visual separation

userStories.title: Status-based card sorting
userStories.description: As a user, I want user stories automatically sorted into the correct column based on their status field so that the board accurately reflects project progress.
acceptanceCriteria: Stories with status incomplete appear in the Incomplete column
Stories with status in-progress appear in the In Progress column
Stories with status complete appear in the Complete column
Unknown status values default to the Incomplete column

userStories.title: File change detection and live updates
userStories.description: As a user, I want the board to automatically update when prd.json files are modified so that I always see the current state without restarting.
acceptanceCriteria: File system watcher monitors all discovered prd.json files using fsnotify
Changes to existing files trigger a re-parse and TUI refresh
Board updates within 2 seconds of file change
TUI remains responsive during file watching

userStories.title: New file detection
userStories.description: As a user, I want newly created prd.json files to be automatically discovered so that new projects appear on the board without restarting the application.
acceptanceCriteria: New prd.json files in existing subdirectories are detected
New subdirectories with prd.json files are detected
New projects appear on the board automatically
Detection occurs within 5 seconds of file creation

userStories.title: Read-only board interface
userStories.description: As a user, I want the board to be read-only so that changes can only be made by editing the prd.json files directly.
acceptanceCriteria: Cards cannot be moved or edited via keyboard or mouse
No edit commands are available in the TUI
Status bar indicates the board is view-only
Helpful message suggests editing prd.json files directly

userStories.title: File deletion handling
userStories.description: As a user, I want projects to be removed from the board when their prd.json file is deleted so that the board stays accurate.
acceptanceCriteria: Deleted prd.json files are detected by the file watcher
Associated project cards are removed from the board
Removal happens automatically without manual intervention
No orphaned cards remain after file deletion

userStories.title: Multi-project aggregation
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see user stories from all discovered projects on a single board so that I have a unified view of all work.
acceptanceCriteria: Cards from multiple prd.json files appear on the same board
Project name on each card distinguishes which project it belongs to
Cards are sorted by status regardless of source project
Board handles at least 20 projects without performance issues

userStories.title: Keyboard navigation
userStories.description: As a user, I want to navigate the board using keyboard shortcuts so that I can efficiently browse user stories.
acceptanceCriteria: Arrow keys or hjkl navigate between cards and columns
Enter or space expands a card to show full description
Tab cycles between columns
q or Ctrl+C quits the application
? displays a help overlay with available shortcuts

userStories.title: Scrollable columns
userStories.description: As a user, I want to scroll within columns when there are more cards than fit on screen so that I can view all user stories.
acceptanceCriteria: Columns are independently scrollable
Scroll position indicator shows current position
Scrolling works via keyboard navigation
Mouse scroll is supported if terminal allows

userStories.title: Graceful exit and cleanup
userStories.description: As a user, I want the application to exit cleanly and restore my terminal state so that my terminal is not left in a broken state.
acceptanceCriteria: Terminal state is restored on exit
File watchers are properly closed
Exit works via q key or Ctrl+C
No zombie processes or resource leaks
